title: COMPLEX*8 is two REAL*4 components — arithmetic ops broadcast over (re, im)
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE COMPLEX_MUL(A, B, C)
C     COMPLEX arithmetic. COMPLEX*8 is two REAL*4 components. AIMAG
C     and REAL extract the parts. The * operator is overloaded to
C     do (a+bi)*(c+di) = (ac-bd) + (ad+bc)i. Java/C# have no built-in
C     COMPLEX -- the rewrite has to provide one (Apache Commons or
C     System.Numerics) or unpack manually. Precision matters: REAL*4
C     parts limit each component to ~7 decimal digits.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      COMPLEX A, B, C
      C = A * B
C     CMPLX(REAL(A)*REAL(B) - AIMAG(A)*AIMAG(B),
C          REAL(A)*AIMAG(B) + AIMAG(A)*REAL(B)) is the unpacked form.
      RETURN
      END
notes: COMPLEX shows up in every Fortran numerical library that touches signal processing or eigenvalue computation. Target languages without native complex types need a library or unpacked components — the spec must surface this so the SME can pick before scaffolding.
